chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' who said:

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a young girl whom her father marries off, then he dies while she is still a minor, and then she grows up before her husband consummates the marriage with her. Is the marriage valid upon her, or is the decision left to her? He said: Her father's marriage of her is valid.

key_terms.الأَمْرُ إِلَيْهَا: The matter/decision is left to her
key_terms.الرُّضَا ع: Al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida
key_terms.يَدخُلَ بِهَا: He enters with her (consummates the marriage)
key_terms.يُزَوِّجُهَا: He marries her off (arranges her marriage)

ai.seo_question: Is a father's marriage arrangement for his minor daughter binding if he dies before consummation?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam Al-Rida (AS), the concept of 'barā'ah' (exemption from the girl's consent) is affirmed, establishing that the father's initial contract remains binding even if he dies before consummation, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence from the Hanafi view. This hadith is central to the debate on 'kafā'ah' and the legal capacity of the father to marry off a minor without her explicit approval, emphasizing the paternal role as the primary guardian in pre-puberty marriages.
